label: What is caused by another is not INFINITE_1, from reception limitation
meaning: Let x have its being caused by some c other than x. By the first premise x is a creature; by the second its esse is received in some principle z; by the third its esse is limited; by the fourth an INFINITE_1 being's esse is not limited, so x is not INFINITE_1. The step from having an external cause of esse to having received esse (kept apart in DISAMB-ESSE-RECEPTION) is carried by two explicit premises, through Creature, not by identifying the two senses. The scope condition of the conclusion binds the first premise in the same way: elements of Being are individuated by their act of being (definition 80dea550), so the divine processions are no instances of CausesIn c x esse with c distinct from x; read with them as instances, the first premise would make the Son a creature. Conditional consequence; the four premises stay open (three supported by q.7 a.1-2 readings, the first bare).
